challenges.title: Show a 12-Month Revenue Trend
challenges.context: The CEO wants to see whether monthly revenue is rising, falling or seasonal across the last year.
challenges.prompt: Which primary visual best serves this decision?
options: Line chart with month on the x-axis and revenue on the y-axis
Pie chart with one slice per month
Single KPI card showing only the latest month
Scatter plot of month number versus row number
challenges.correctOption: Line chart with month on the x-axis and revenue on the y-axis
hints: The x-axis has a natural time order.
The decision depends on change over time.
A line chart makes trend and seasonality visible.
challenges.explanation: Line charts encode ordered time naturally and make direction, turning points and seasonality easier to see than part-to-whole charts.

challenges.title: Define the Retention KPI
challenges.context: A SaaS manager asks whether customers acquired in each month keep using the product over later months.
challenges.prompt: Which KPI design is most defensible?
options: Cohort retention: percentage of each acquisition cohort active in each later period
Total signups since company launch
Average employee age
Raw page views without a customer denominator
challenges.correctOption: Cohort retention: percentage of each acquisition cohort active in each later period
hints: The question is about behavior after acquisition.
Different acquisition months need comparable denominators.
Cohorts preserve the starting population for retention analysis.
challenges.explanation: Cohort retention compares like-with-like populations and prevents growth in new signups from hiding deterioration in existing-customer behavior.

challenges.title: Catch a Misleading Bar Chart
challenges.context: A dashboard shows product A at 98 satisfaction and product B at 96, but the bar-axis starts at 95 so A looks several times taller.
challenges.prompt: What is the main design risk?
options: The truncated axis exaggerates a small absolute difference
Bars can never display percentages
The chart needs more decorative colors
The data must be causal because it is visualized
challenges.correctOption: The truncated axis exaggerates a small absolute difference
hints: Compare the numeric difference with the visual difference.
Bar length is interpreted from a baseline.
Starting near 95 magnifies a two-point gap.
challenges.explanation: For bars, a zero baseline usually protects proportional interpretation. A truncated baseline can visually overstate small differences.

challenges.title: Design the Executive Landing Page
challenges.context: The CEO has five minutes each Monday. The analytics team currently shows 42 charts on one page.
options: Lead with a small set of decision KPIs and exceptions, then allow drill-down into diagnostic detail
Keep all 42 charts so no information is omitted
Replace all numbers with decorative gauges
Show raw transaction rows first
challenges.correctOption: Lead with a small set of decision KPIs and exceptions, then allow drill-down into diagnostic detail
hints: The first page should answer what changed and where action is needed.
Details can exist behind drill-down rather than competing for attention.
challenges.explanation: A strong executive dashboard establishes hierarchy: headline outcomes, exceptions and actionable drivers first; diagnostic detail remains available without overwhelming the landing view.

challenges.title: Choose the Checkout KPI Set
challenges.context: E-commerce revenue fell. Product traffic is stable, so leadership wants to know whether checkout behavior changed.
challenges.prompt: Which KPI set best diagnoses the funnel?
options: Product view→cart rate, cart→checkout rate, checkout→purchase rate, plus counts at each stage
Only total website page views
Only total revenue
Employee headcount by office
Number of dashboard users
challenges.correctOption: Product view→cart rate, cart→checkout rate, checkout→purchase rate, plus counts at each stage
hints: A total outcome alone cannot locate the leaking stage.
Rates need their underlying counts for context.
Measure each transition in the funnel.
challenges.explanation: Stage counts plus transition rates identify where loss occurs and prevent a single top-line KPI from hiding the mechanism.
